Hi Logan,

Thanks for sending the initial SIG spreadsheet last week. Our InfoSec team reviewed section 6 (Data Handling) and asked for a few clarifications before we can move to legal: specifically

- Do you persist full prompt logs? If so, for how long and can retention be configured per customer?
- Are prompt logs or generated outputs used to train Redwood models (or downstream models)? If yes, what opt-out controls exist?
- What elements are redacted or tokenized when you retain logs (e.g., PII fields) and how do you document lineage?

They also requested any attestation or evidence we can attach to the SIG (SOC 2 summary, answers, and a simple diagram of the logging/retention flow). Can you provide those by EOD Monday?

Logan/Monica,

Draft responses below — I kept answers short for the SIG spreadsheet and attached the SOC 2 summary + a one-page retention flow diagram. Please review; happy to expand any bullet for MediCore's legal team.

1) Prompt/log persistence and retention- We persist request/response logs in our production telemetry to support SLOs, debugging, and abuse detection. Retention defaults to 90 days for hosted customers.
- Retention is configurable on dedicated/private deployments and can be extended or shortened via contract for Dedicated or Private arrangements. For hosted accounts, we offer a contractual retention addendum for enterprise customers (we can commit to custom retention windows for an agreed term).
- Customers can request expedited deletion; deletion requests are processed within 5 business days for hosted API data and within the committed SLA window for Dedicated/Private installations.

2) Use for model training- By default, Redwood does not use customer-provided prompts or generated outputs from paid customer environments to train our public model weights.
- For hosted trial or community-contributed data, we have explicit opt-in mechanisms and anonymization pipelines; customer data used for research/training requires documented consent.
- For Dedicated and Private customers, training on customer data is off by default and only performed under explicit customer agreement (we include language in the MSA).

3) Redaction, lineage, and what we store- We store raw event records (headers, timestamps, token counts, model id, request/response text) for the retention period noted above.
- PII handling: we offer automated PII detection for labeling and optional automated redaction pipelines. Redaction is configurable and can be applied prior to long-term retention.
- Lineage: each persisted event includes metadata linking to request id, model version, and route. We provide audit logs and an exportable CSV for customers upon request; for Private deployments customers have direct access to logs.

Evidence attached: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (SOC 2 scope and auditor statement) and prompt-log-retention-diagram.png (visual flow of ingestion -> short-term store -> ephemeral KV cache -> optional long-term retention).

Notes: I added a short paragraph you can paste into the SIG cell about training and opt-out. If MediCore wants a contractual assurance (no-training clause), Legal should review the MSA amendment.

Mina Haddad

Julie / Daniel,

Thanks for the clear list — see our consolidated answers below and the attached evidence bundle (SOC 2 summary + SIG spreadsheet with our responses). Short version up top and details in the spreadsheet.

Quick answers
- Do you persist full prompt logs? Yes — request/response records are persisted to support SRE, debugging, and abuse detection. Default hosted retention is 90 days; retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private and negotiable via contract.
- Are prompts/outputs used to train models? No for paid customer environments by default. Any use of customer data for training requires explicit opt-in/consent and will be documented in the contract.
- Redaction/lineage? We provide automated PII detection and optional redaction before long-term retention. Each event contains metadata (request id, model version, route) so we can provide provenance and audit exports.

- redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (summary of SOC 2 scope and auditor attestation)
